title: Waiting state
body:
A [[Processes|process]] is in the waiting state when it is blocked on something that has
not happened yet, so the scheduler will not consider it at all. It sits in a
[[Wait Queue]] rather than the [[Ready Queue]].

Things you wait on:

- I/O completing (disk, network, a key being pressed)
- a [[Semaphores|semaphore]] whose counter is 0, so `sem_wait` blocks
- a child process exiting
- a message arriving, in [[Message Passing]]

The mechanism from [[Semaphores]]: acquire a lock when the counter is already 0 and you go
into the waiting state; the process that releases it increments the counter *and* signals
you, which moves you to the ready queue. You do not resume on the spot, see
[[Process State]].

**Waiting costs you the CPU, and that is the point.** A waiting process is off the CPU
entirely, so the time is not wasted. Compare a [[Spin Lock]], which stays Running and burns
the CPU checking a flag. Blocking is right when the wait is long, spinning is right when
the wait is shorter than the two [[Context Switching|context switches]] blocking would
cost.
